title: Extra Charge for Tile and Grout Deep Cleaning? How to Tell If It's in Your Base Contract
seoTitle: Extra Charge Tile and Grout Deep Cleaning: Included or Add-On?
metaDescription: Extra charge tile and grout deep cleaning explained: when it's folded into base retainers vs billed at $0.75–$2.50/sq ft. Audit bids in our comparator.
excerpt: Many office managers discover tile and grout deep scrubbing is excluded from their janitorial contract only when the first work-order invoice arrives. This audit guide shows how to read scope language, compare bundled and add-on pricing, and negotiate the right structure.
quickAnswer: Standard nightly janitorial contracts almost never include true tile and grout deep scrubbing; they cover damp mopping only, and deep scrubbing is billed as a separate work order at roughly $0.75–$2.50 per sq ft with a $250–$450 minimum. Some vendors fold a quarterly scrub into the base retainer, which usually adds about $0.03–$0.06 per sq ft per month to the contract, so the real question is whether the scope names the task, frequency, and square footage in writing.

blocks.text: Why Tile and Grout Is the Most Disputed Line in Janitorial Scopes

Janitorial proposals often say restroom floors cleaned nightly or hard floors mopped and maintained. To the buyer, that sounds like the floors will stay clean. To the vendor, it means a damp mop with neutral cleaner. Damp mopping removes surface soil from the tile face but leaves compacted soil in grout joints, so within six to twelve months the grout darkens and the buyer asks why. The vendor then quotes a deep scrub as extra work, and the dispute begins. Clear scope language prevents that conversation.
Three Ways Vendors Structure Tile and Grout Work

blocks.caption: Included vs. add-on structures for tile and grout deep scrubbing
rows: $0.75 – $2.50 per sq ft per visit; $250 – $450 minimum
Easy to defer until restoration pricing applies
Fixed price per scrub on a set calendar
$0.75 – $1.25 per sq ft per scrub, often 10–15% below ad hoc
Predictable, still visible as its own line
Requires you to track visits were performed
Adds about $0.03 – $0.06 per sq ft per month of total building area
Hard to verify; visits can quietly be skipped

blocks.text: As a reference point, a 12,000 sq ft office paying $0.10 per sq ft per visit for twice-weekly service spends about $1,200 per visit times 8.66 visits, or roughly $10,392 per month. Bundling a quarterly tile program might add $360–$720 per month to that retainer. If the office has only 800 sq ft of tile, an add-on line at $1.00 per sq ft quarterly costs $3,200 a year, or $267 per month, which is cheaper than the bundled range. Bundling makes more sense when tile is a larger share of the floor plate.

items: Excluded indicators: phrases like periodic services quoted separately, project work billed at time and materials, or floor restoration not included.
Partial inclusion: restroom floors machine-scrubbed monthly may mean an orbital pass without grout-specific chemistry or wet recovery.
True inclusion: tile and grout deep scrubbed quarterly in restrooms (1,100 sq ft) and breakroom (300 sq ft) using alkaline grout cleaner, machine agitation, and wet-vac recovery.
Sealer: almost always excluded unless named; treat any silence on sealing as exclusion.
Verification: inclusion is only enforceable if the contract requires dated service tickets or before-and-after photos.

blocks.title: The silent-skip risk in bundled retainers
blocks.text: When deep scrubbing is buried in the monthly fee, a vendor under margin pressure may push or skip visits without a price change. Require the vendor to submit a work ticket with date, zones, and square footage for every periodic service, and reserve the right to a credit for any missed visit.
Audit Procedure for an Existing Contract

items.name: Pull the scope of work exhibit
items.text: Find the task frequency schedule, usually an exhibit or appendix, rather than relying on the proposal summary.

items.name: Search for floor verbs
items.text: Look for mop, scrub, machine scrub, extract, detail, and seal. Only scrub with recovery or extract indicates deep grout work.

items.name: Check periodic and exclusion sections
items.text: Many contracts list deep scrubbing under periodic services with a separate rate sheet or under exclusions entirely.

items.name: Match to invoices
items.text: Compare 12 months of invoices against the schedule to see whether bundled scrubs were ever performed or billed twice.

items.name: Request a rate sheet
items.text: Even if work is bundled, ask for the per-sq-ft rate the vendor uses so you can value credits and compare competitors.

blocks.text: How Consumables Clauses Signal Scope Philosophy

Vendors that bundle aggressively often bundle consumables as well. If your contract includes restroom paper and liners, typically $0.012–$0.025 per sq ft per visit in our benchmarks, check whether those products are named by spec. A scope that specifies EcoLogo-certified 2-ply jumbo bath tissue on 9-inch, 1,000 ft rolls like Tork Universal, 38x60 inch 17-micron 55-gallon liners such as Berry Rhino-X for breakroom wet waste, and multifold towels like Pacific Blue Basic in 4,000-count cases is a vendor that writes precise scopes. Those vendors are also more likely to define tile work precisely. Vague consumables language often travels with vague floor-care language.

If tile is less than 10% of your floor area, ask for a scheduled add-on line with a fixed per-sq-ft rate and a set calendar. If tile exceeds 15–20%, for example in medical-office or food-service tenant buildings, bundling can be efficient as long as verification is written in. In both cases, cap restorative pricing: a clause stating that scheduled scrubs will be billed at the maintenance rate protects you from a vendor letting grout deteriorate and then charging restoration rates.

blocks.title: Insurance and chemical documentation for add-on work
blocks.text: Separate work orders are sometimes performed by a subcontracted floor crew. Require that any subcontractor carry its own certificate of insurance naming your company and landlord as additional insureds, and that SDS sheets for grout chemicals are provided under OSHA HazCom before work starts.

faqs.q: Is tile and grout scrubbing ever part of standard janitorial service?
faqs.a: Rarely as true deep cleaning. Standard service covers sweeping and damp mopping. A minority of premium contracts bundle quarterly scrubbing, but it must be named with frequency and footage to count. If the scope only says floors cleaned, assume deep scrubbing will carry an extra charge.

faqs.q: How do I convert a bundled tile program into a comparable number?
faqs.a: Ask the vendor how much of the monthly fee is attributable to periodic floor care. Multiply by 12 and divide by scrubs per year to get a per-visit cost, then divide by tiled square footage. Compare that to $0.75–$1.25 per sq ft maintenance pricing.

faqs.q: Can I add tile scrubbing mid-contract without rebidding?
faqs.a: Usually yes, through a change order. Get the rate, frequency, zones, and footage in a signed amendment. Ensure the amendment references the original insurance and indemnity terms and does not reset contract term or auto-renewal dates.

faqs.q: Do green cleaning requirements affect add-on pricing?
faqs.a: They can. If your policy requires Green Seal GS-37 or ECOLOGO-certified chemistry, some vendors charge slightly more for longer dwell or additional passes on heavy soil. Specify the requirement before bidding so every vendor prices the same chemistry.

faqs.q: What if my vendor says grout restoration is needed after years of bundled service?
faqs.a: Review whether the bundled scrubs were actually performed. If service tickets are missing, you have grounds to request the restoration at maintenance pricing or as a credit. That is why verification language is essential in any bundled agreement.
